title: DocOverlay
description: AI-authored documentation overlay (Tier 2) for an okapi-bridge filter or step. This is the durable, committed home of all AI-generated prose — overview, worked examples, and per-parameter help — kept SEPARATE from Okapi-extracted facts (Tier 1: schema/introspection) and human curation (Tier 3: overrides). Every overlay file must declare its provenance so the reference site can show what is Okapi-provided versus AI-generated. Grounded in the Okapi Java source and (where available) the Okapi wiki — never invented.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, e.g. '../overlay.schema.json'.

id.description: Capability id. Filters use the okf_ prefix (e.g. 'okf_basetable'); steps use the kebab schema id (e.g. 'exact-match-word-count').

kind.description: Whether this overlay documents a filter (format) or a step (tool).

name.description: Human-readable name (e.g. 'Comma-Separated Values Filter', 'Exact Match Word Count Step').

overview.description: 2-4 sentence markdown overview: what this filter/step does, what it handles, and its primary use case. Restrained academic register — no marketing superlatives, no emoji, no hardcoded counts.

limitations.description: Known limitations, each a concise markdown statement grounded in the Okapi implementation.

processingNotes.description: Important processing behaviors (encoding/BOM handling, segmentation dependence, annotations emitted, performance). Each a concise markdown statement.

description.description: Markdown explanation of what the example demonstrates.

config.description: Configuration snippet as a fenced markdown code block (```yaml / ```json). Null if not applicable.

input.description: Input content as a fenced markdown code block. Null if not applicable.

output.description: Expected output as a fenced markdown code block. Null if not applicable.

examples.description: Worked examples showing configuration and/or input/output patterns.

parameters.description: Per-parameter help keyed by the composite-schema property path. Use the dotted group path (e.g. 'extraction.extractAll') OR the leaf name ('extractAll') — gen-refs matches either. Do NOT repeat the title/type/default (those are Tier 1 schema facts).

help.description: Behavioral/usage help in markdown. Explain BEHAVIOR and USAGE, not the title or type.

values.description: Markdown description of valid values/ranges/format. Null if the schema constraints are self-explanatory.

notes.description: Warnings/caveats/tips from the source or wiki.

examples.description: Short inline examples (e.g. regex patterns, paths).

dependsOn.description: Semantic dependencies not captured by x-editor.enabledBy (overrides/conflicts/only-meaningful-when).

introducedIn.description: Okapi version where the parameter was introduced.

propertySuggestions.description: Suggested title/description for schema properties missing them (consumed by apply-property-suggestions).

fullDoc.description: Optional complete self-contained markdown documentation page.

wikiUrl.description: Source Okapi wiki page, when one exists. Empty/omitted for programmatic capabilities with no wiki.

aliasOf.description: For sub-configuration formats: the parent filter id whose overlay this one specialises (e.g. okf_commaseparatedvalues -> okf_table). When set, compose-docs starts from the parent overlay and applies this file's fields as a tailored delta. Mirrors an entry in aliases.json.

x-provenance.description: Provenance for the AI-authored content in this file. Makes the Okapi-vs-AI boundary auditable.

generator.description: What produced this content: a model id (e.g. 'claude-opus-4-7'), 'claude/wiki-parse' (migrated from the wiki-parse pipeline), or 'human' if hand-written from scratch.

model.description: Specific model id if generator is generic.

grounding.description: Evidence the content is grounded in, not invented. Each entry is a source ref: 'okapi-source:okapi/steps/wordcount/.../ExactMatchWordCountStep.java', 'wiki:<url>', or 'schema' (composite schema for this id). At least one required.

authoredAt.description: ISO date the content was authored/migrated.

reviewed.description: True once a human (Tier 3) has reviewed the AI content. Drives the 'reviewed' vs 'unreviewed AI' badge.
